newsitem.title: UK: FSU key driver of 1998 oil demand growth - IEA.
newsitem.headline: FSU key driver of 1998 oil demand growth - IEA.

text.p: An expected turnaround in former Soviet Union oil demand from a small decline in 1997 to modest growth in 1998 will be a key driver of accelerated global demand growth next year, helping to offset declines in other regions, the International Energy Agency said on Friday.

World oil demand growth in 1998 should reach 2.5 percent, adding 1.85 million barrels per day (bpd) to this year's 73.68 million bpd, slightly surpassing the 1.75 million bpd growth in 1997 over 1996, the IEA said in its monthly Oil Market Report.

Demand growth will remain concentrated in non-OECD countries, where consumption is set to rise by 4.2 percent or 1.3 million bpd to 33.4 million bpd, very slightly higher than 1997's expected growth rate.

"The projection includes a minor slowdown in oil demand growth in most non-OECD regions, including Other Asia (excluding China) and Latin America, offset by an assumed return to modest oil demand growth in the FSU," the report said.

The IEA, which monitors oil market trends for members of the OECD, also said it had revised upwards its assessment of apparent demand in the former Soviet Union in the second and third quarters of 1997.
Apparent demand -- derived from production minus net oil exports -- is expected to increase by three percent in the second quarter and decrease by 2.8 percent in the third quarter.
After the revisions, overall demand this year is projected to decline by 0.4 percent or 20,000 bpd to 4.3 million bpd.
Booming Chinese demand is also set to play a key role in supporting global demand growth this year and next.

In March, Chinese total net crude imports almost doubled month-on-month to a record 962,000 bpd, 163 percent up on year-earlier levels. Indonesia, West Africa and Alaska were China's main suppliers, the IEA said.
